title: Arjuna meets his son in battle
hookLine: the sacrificial horse reaches Manipura, and the young king who comes out to meet Arjuna is his own son
carry: svadharma: do the duty of the role you're in
tomorrow: the great sacrifice is done. why is a half-golden mongoose unimpressed?

lines: HIS SON COMES OUT WITH GIFTS.
cards: The horse has been set loose at last. It wanders where it likes, and Arjuna follows with his bow, country after country, fighting the kings who challenge it. Then it walks into Manipura.
Long ago, on his travels, Arjuna married a princess of this land, Chitrangada, and left a son here. That son, Babhruvahana, is king now.
And he comes out of the city to meet the horse, not with an army but with gifts and brahmanas, his head bowed to his father.

teach.b: Arjuna is angry. In Ganguli's telling he scolds his son: I've come as a warrior guarding a sacrificial horse, and you greet me like this? A king of your order should fight.
Then someone rises out of the earth: Ulupi, the serpent princess, another of Arjuna's wives.

teach.h: THE SON'S ARROW FELLS THE FATHER
teach.b: Do what your father asks, she tells the young king. Fight him. So father and son meet in battle, and the son is very good.
His arrow strikes Arjuna, and Arjuna falls and does not get up. Then Ulupi places a gem from the serpent world on Arjuna's chest, and he wakes as if from sleep.

teach.h: A GEM, AND AN OLD CURSE LIFTED
teach.b: She explains: when Arjuna brought Bhishma down from behind Shikhandi, the Vasus, Bhishma's divine brothers, cursed him, and the curse was to end at his own son's hands. Today it did. Now the teaching underneath.
Hindus call it svadharma, your own duty, and it changes with the role you're standing in. As a son, Babhruvahana bows.

teach.h: BOW AS SON, RIDE AS KING
teach.b: As the king whose land the horse has entered, he must ride out. Arjuna knows this from the inside.

teach.h: SVADHARMA: THE DUTY OF YOUR ROLE
teach.b: Before the war he begged not to fight his own grandfather and teacher, and Krishna told him in the Gita: better your own dharma, done imperfectly, than another's done well. Now the student of the Gita says it to his son.
Many teachers read the scene as the Gita coming home, and the duty done fully is what frees Arjuna.

how: Arjuna's encounter with Babhruvahana is told in the Ashvamedhika Parva and retold in Indian theater and storytelling; teachers often set it beside Krishna's call to svadharma in the Gita.

o: the book of the horse Arjuna guards on its travels
the serpent world where Ulupi's people live
a curse that divine beings lay on a warrior

games.q: father and son at Manipura — tap the pairs.
p: came out with gifts, then fought
urged the fight and brought the gem

s: Arjuna is pleased when his son greets him peacefully
he scolds him: as a king guarding his land, his duty is to fight.
the son is the one who fells the father.
Arjuna once told Krishna he couldn't fight his own elders
before the war, in the Gita; now he tells his son to do his duty as a king.

games.q: you're Babhruvahana. as a son you bowed. now your father says the king of this land should meet the horse's guardian in battle. by svadharma, what fits?
o: fight him: as king, defending your land is your duty today.
keep bowing: a son's duty always comes first.
hand the fight to your generals.
games.why: Babhruvahana bowed as a son, then fought as a king when Arjuna named that his duty, and his arrow ended the Vasus' curse. svadharma: each role asks its own duty.

practice: Put your palms together and picture a parent or an elder in front of you. Bow to them a little, the way Babhruvahana bowed and the way many Hindus greet an elder with pranam, touching their feet.
Then name one role you'll stand in today, where you may have to speak up or hold your ground, even with someone you respect.
If you pray, ask for the strength to do that duty well; if you don't, just hold both, the bow and the duty.

wordCard.voice: Ashvamedhika. The book where a father, following the horse, is struck down by his own son and brought back by a serpent princess's gem.

orig.note: Ulupi: the serpent princess, Arjuna's wife, who urges the fight and revives him.

carryVoice: Your line: svadharma, do the duty of the role you're in. The son's arrow ended the father's curse. Day eight hundred seventy-one.

sources.ref: Mahabharata, Ashvamedhika Parva, Arjuna and Babhruvahana at Manipura: the rebuke, Ulupi's urging, the battle, Chitrangada's lament, the gem and the curse of the Vasus
Bhagavad Gita 2.4 (Arjuna asks how he can fight Bhishma and Drona) and 3.35 (better one's own dharma, though imperfect, than another's well done)
